title: Tutorial: Read a Module Output
scenario: A module can expose values to its caller through outputs. The caller reads them with module.<name>.<output>. Wire a module output to a root output so operators can see it.
constraints: Keep the module storage call unchanged.

focus.title: Wire the module output
focus.todo: Set the root output value to the module's storage_id output.

hints.why: Outputs are the contract between a module and its caller. They prevent a caller from depending on internal resource addresses, which the module should be free to change.
hints.what: Complete the root output value. The module is already called; the only missing piece is the dotted reference that reaches its exported storage_id.
hints.when: Use a module output when a caller needs an identifier or setting without knowing how the module implements it.
hints.how: Inside the existing root `output` block, set `value` to the module output reference. Use the module label from the `module` block and the exported name `storage_id` from the module's `outputs.tf`, joined with dots.

test_manifest.title: the output reads the module output
